sources.entry: Typesense - Blazing fast, typo-tolerant open source search engine optimized for developer happiness and ease of use. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C++/Docker/K8S/deb

summary.one_liner: Typesense is an open-source, typo-tolerant search engine server written in C++, positioned as a simpler alternative to Algolia and Elasticsearch.
summary.what_it_does: Typesense runs as a single self-contained native server binary that stores collections of JSON documents and answers search queries over HTTP. Clients create a collection with typed fields, index documents, and search with parameters such as query fields, filters, and sort order. Typo tolerance is built in and enabled by default. The README also mentions faceting, geosearch, and type-ahead/spellchecker demos, plus semantic and hybrid search on a demo dataset. Official API clients are listed for JavaScript, PHP, Python, and Ruby, with community clients for several other languages. Building from source uses Bazel and requires C++11, Snappy, zlib, OpenSSL, curl, and ICU.
use_cases: add typo-tolerant search to a website or app
search a large product or catalog dataset
how_to_run: Create a collection with the Python client (see Quick Start), then index a document and search it
notable: Single lightweight native binary, positioned against the JVM-based Elasticsearch
Typo tolerance works out of the box without tuning
Search-time query parameters instead of fixed per-index settings, and sorted results from a single index
README states a fresh server uses about 30 MB of memory; 1M Hacker News titles use about 165 MB
Official clients use a built-in retry strategy for HA setups
caveats: Server is GPL-3.0 licensed; the README explains the choice and notes client libraries are Apache-licensed
Personalization and server-side search analytics are listed as not currently available
Managed hosting (Typesense Cloud) and paid support are offered separately
